name: CAM.P

functions.note: LED strobe, frame interrupt, frame sync or external clock (one at a time); unused by the driver
I2C address strap, latched 30 ms after power-up: floating 0x35 (default), to VDDIO 0x25, to GND 0x40. The broadcast address 0x60 always answers too.

power.notes: V+ feeds the camera I/O (VDDIO) directly, and its 3.3 V analog supply through a TPS610995 boost (3.6 V) and TPS7A2033 LDO. About 0.7 mA while streaming at 30 fps from 3.3 V, about 1 mA from 1.8 V.

headline: monochrome QVGA camera
description: An ultra-low-power machine-vision tile built around the PixArt PAG7920J3, a 320 × 240 monochrome global-shutter camera module with an integrated lens. It captures 8-bit RAW frames over SPI (30 fps as configured; the chip's 180 fps is a parallel-bus figure), with 3.0 µm pixels, a 71.3° × 53.7° field of view, and 64 dB of dynamic range. Configuration is over I2C. A proprietary on-chip motion-detection mode draws under 100 µW (compared to 760 µW for QVGA output at 15 fps) making the tile practical to leave always-on in a battery-powered system, with auto exposure and gain control, auto black cancellation, mirror/flip, windowing, LED strobe, and multi-sensor frame sync built in.

application_notes.details: when GPIO2 (pad 3) is left floating, the I2C address will default to 0x35.  Pulling GPIO2 (pad 3) high will change the address to 0x25, while grounding pad 3 will set it to 0x40.  The camera will also respond to general broadcasts on 0x60.
